description:
FILED s484a (Opus, 2026-09-13), found while writing #1628's guard rows -- the
first draft spelled its fixtures `\(my $hr = \%h)` and two rows would not die.
PRE-EXISTING: identical on main 2ffefb36 and on the s484a tree (probe
scratch/s484a/probes/w1628.pl run on both).

THE DECLARATION SPELLING CHANGES THE ANSWER, which is the finding:

    use strict; use warnings;
    my %h = (k=>"v"); my $hrr = \(my $hr = \%h);     # <-- decl inside \( )
    my @a = (10,11);  my $arr = \(my $ar = \@a);
    print ref($hr), ref($hrr), ref($ar), ref($arr), "\n";
    print eval { scalar @$hr } // "undef", " [", ($@?"ERR":""), "]\n";
    print eval { scalar keys %$ar } // "undef", " [", ($@?"ERR":""), "]\n";

    perl 5.40.3:  HASH REF ARRAY REF
                  undef [ERR]        Not an ARRAY reference
                  undef [ERR]        Not a HASH reference
    PCL        :  HASH REF ARRAY REF      <-- ref() is RIGHT
                  1     []                <-- @$hr  is the referent box, read
                                              as a ONE-ELEMENT LIST
                  2     []                <-- keys %$ar counts the array's
                                              elements as keys

The TWO-STATEMENT spelling of exactly the same program

    my %h = (k=>"v"); my $hr = \%h; my $hrr = \$hr;
    my @a = (10,11);  my $ar = \@a; my $arr = \$ar;

dies correctly on both (`Not an ARRAY reference` / `Not a HASH reference`),
so this is not the wrong-kind rule -- that rule works.  What differs is the
BOX SHAPE `$hr` ends up with when the declaration is the operand of `\`:
`ref($hr)` answers HASH, so the representation still carries the reference,
but `(unbox $hr)` evidently leaves a p-box where the plain spelling leaves
the hash table, so `p-cast-@`'s `((p-box-p v) (unbox v))` layer-peel fires
and hands the caller something it reads as a list of one.

NOT ABOUT #1628: the ref-to-ref halves of this same probe (`@$arr`, `%$hrr`)
DO die on the s484a tree (they are #1628's fix) and did not on the base, so
the two are independent.  `\(my $x = EXPR)` is the only shape measured; the
sibling spellings to probe are `\(our $x = â¦)`, `\(my ($a,$b) = â¦)` (a LIST,
where perl gives a ref per element), `\(state $x = â¦)` and a `\(my $x)` with
no initialiser.

WHERE TO LOOK: what `p-backslash` / the `my`-declaration lowering produce for
a declaration used as `\`'s operand -- specifically whether the wrapper ends
up holding the DECLARATION's box (correct) or an extra layer.  The clean test
is a one-line comparison of the emission for the two spellings.

BAR: ~8 probes vs perl (the four sibling spellings above plus the element
accesses `$$hr{k}` / `$$ar[0]`, which are NOT broken and must stay right),
guard rows in Pl/t/ref-to-ref-01.t beside the #1628 block (whose header
comment already points here), the full sweep if the fix is in `cl/`, or
corpus-diff + emission-ab if it is in the emitter.
SIZE: S-M.
subject: a scalar declared INSIDE `\(my $hr = \%h)` loses the wrong-kind whole-aggregate fatal: `@$hr` answers 1 and `%$ar` answers 2 where perl dies, while the two-statement spelling of the same code dies correctly
